title: Hot-path cache replay provenance and fidelity evaluation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Build a reproducible eval and monitoring harness that attributes output fidelity regressions to hot-path KV/prefix cache artifacts (cache entry provenance + config/model changes) and produce an actionable signal for rollout gating.

Background: We've seen intermittent semantic shifts correlated with cache hits when model or config changes land. Existing suites surface end-to-end deltas but do not attach provenance to cache entries or quantify how much of the delta is attributable to cached state vs downstream model nondeterminism. This ticket designs and implements a provenance-aware replay harness and a compact fidelity metric to drive alerts and canary gates.

Approach:
1) Instrument cache entries with immutable provenance metadata: upstream model-version, config-fingerprint (quantization/compilation flags), request-fingerprint (prompt hash + tokenizer version), sequence-length-bucket, and creation timestamp.
2) Implement a hot-path replay tracer: when a live request hits the cache, record a lightweight trace (entry_id, provenance metadata, hit_offset, token-count) and also capture the unconditional partial-generation logprobs (stream-sampled).
3) Replay experiment framework: for each sampled request create three runs: (A) production hit path (with cache), (B) forced-miss baseline (cache bypass but same model/config), (C) forced-miss with prior-model (when applicable) to isolate model-change impact.
4) Fidelity metric (Prefix-Fidelity-Index): composite score combining embedding-similarity (cosine), n-gram overlap (ROUGE-L), and token-level logprob delta normalized by prompt length. Produce per-request score and cohort summaries (median, 95th percentile, drift rate).
5) Noise modeling: estimate nondeterministic variance by repeated replay of baseline runs to set adaptive thresholds and avoid false positives.
6) Alerting & rollout gate: surface per-route and per-model fingerprints that exceed drift thresholds in Console. Integrate with canary rollout automation: fail canary if cohort-level Prefix-Fidelity-Index drops below threshold or if >X% of golden anchors exceed divergence.

Implementation notes: prefer instrumentation that does not change cache lookup latency: provenance metadata appended to entry during creation and recorded asynchronously to the tracing store. Replays should run in background namespace with token-limited sampling.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Risks & mitigations:
- Volume: sampling rate must be tuned to contain storage/compute costs; start with 0.1% global sample and route-weighting.
- Privacy: request-fingerprint must be a one-way hash with no raw prompt storage; redaction policy must be enforced for PII-heavy routes.
- False positives from nondeterminism: baseline repeated-run variance estimation required.

Operational outputs: new Console dashboard panels (per-route provenance heatmap), alert playbook, canary gating policy, public runbook for triage teams.

acceptance_criteria: Provenance metadata is stored with every cache entry and visible in trace records within 24 hours of rollout
Replay harness can run A/B/C comparisons for sampled requests with <5s scheduling latency and stores outputs in the tracing store
Prefix-Fidelity-Index computed for each sampled request and cohort-level dashboards updated in Console (median + 95th)
Noise-modeling reduces false positive rate: baseline repeated-run variance explains >95% of observed delta under stable model/config
Alerting rules trigger when cohort Prefix-Fidelity-Index crosses configured thresholds and can block canary promotion via existing rollout automation
Privacy constraints satisfied: raw prompts are not stored in tracing store; fingerprints are one-way hashes and documented in security review
